records.literal_gloss: [Have] not you seen what the people the this have spoken, saying, [the] two the clans which chose Yahweh in them, and he has rejected them? And my people they despise, from being again a nation before them.

en.L: "Have you not seen what this people have spoken, saying, 'The two clans that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chose, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has rejected them'? And they despise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, [as] no longer a nation before them.
en.B: "Have you not seen what these people are saying: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chose two families, and now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has rejected them'? So they look down on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, as if they were no longer a nation in their eyes.
en.R: "Have you heard what these people are saying? They say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chose two families, Israel and Judah, but now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has turned away from them.' So they treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people with scorn. They do not think of them as a nation anymore.

es.L: «¿No has visto lo que ha hablado este pueblo, diciendo: “Las dos familias que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} escogió, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} las ha desechado”? Y desprecian a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, [como si] no fuera más nación delante de ellos.
es.B: «¿No has visto lo que dice esta gente: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} escogió a dos familias, y ahora las ha desechado”? Así desprecian a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, como si ya no fuera una nación a sus ojos.
es.R: «¿Has oído lo que dice esta gente? Dicen: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} escogió a dos familias, Israel y Judá, pero ahora les ha dado la espalda”. Así tratan con desprecio a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. Ya no lo consideran una nación.

sw.L: "Je, hujaona yale ambayo watu hawa wameyanena, wakisema, 'Jamaa mbili ambazo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alizichagua, amezikataa'? Nao wanawadharau watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, [kana kwamba] si taifa tena mbele yao.
sw.B: "Je, hujaona wanachosema watu hawa: '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alichagua jamaa mbili, na sasa amezikataa'? Hivyo wanawadharau watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kana kwamba si taifa tena machoni pao.
sw.R: "Je, umesikia wanachosema watu hawa? Wanasema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alichagua jamaa mbili, Israeli na Yuda, lakini sasa amewaacha.' Kwa hiyo wanawadharau watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Hawawahesabu tena kuwa taifa.

decisions.choice: the two families: Israel and Judah
alternatives: the house of David and the Levites
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a clan, here used of whole peoples, as in Amos 3:1-2, where all Israel is "the whole family" God brought up from Egypt. The two are most likely the two kingdoms, Israel and Judah (3:6-11; 11:10). Some take them as David's line and the Levites, the two chosen houses of verses 17-22, or as Jacob's descendants and David's (verse 26).

decisions.choice: this people: who are speaking is not said
decisions.reason: "This people" in Jeremiah is often Judah itself (14:10-11), and the words may be the people's own despair. But the end of the verse says that "they" despise "my people", which suggests outsiders, perhaps the neighboring nations, mocking them. The Hebrew leaves it open.

decisions.choice: chosen and rejected: the language of covenant
decisions.reason: God chose Israel to be his own people (Deuteronomy 7:6; 14:2). The speakers say that he has now rejected them, as he had warned (7:29; 2 Kings 17:20). God's answer in verses 25-26 is that he will not.

decisions.choice: no longer a nation before them: in their eyes no nation at all
decisions.reason: "Before them" means in their view. They count God's people as finished.

decisions.choice: clans (L); families (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "clans", the usual word for this term. Balanced and Readable say "families", because here the word names whole nations, and "clans" would sound too small.

decisions.choice: two families, Israel and Judah
decisions.reason: Readable names the two families as Israel and Judah, following m1. This is the likeliest meaning, but not certain.

source.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם־לֹ֥א בְרִיתִ֖י יוֹמָ֣ם וָלָ֑יְלָה חֻקּ֛וֹת שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָ֖רֶץ לֹא־שָֽׂמְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: if not my covenant [with] daytime and night, [the] fixed laws of heavens and earth not I have set,

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: If [there is] not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with day and night, [if] I have not set the fixed laws of heaven and earth,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: If I had not made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with day and night, if I had not set in place the fixed laws of heaven and earth,
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I have made a covenant with day and night. I have set the laws that the sky and the earth must follow. They still stand.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Si no [existe] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto con el día y la noche, [si] no he puesto las leyes fijas del cielo y de la tierra,
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Si yo no hubiera hecho {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto con el día y la noche, si no hubiera establecido las leyes fijas del cielo y de la tierra,
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Yo hice un pacto con el día y la noche. Establecí las leyes que el cielo y la tierra deben seguir. Esas leyes siguen firmes.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Kama [hakuna] agano {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} na mchana na usiku, [kama] sikuziweka amri za mbingu na nchi,
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Kama nisingefanya agano {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} na mchana na usiku, kama nisingeziweka amri za kudumu za mbingu na nchi,
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Nimefanya agano na mchana na usiku. Nimeweka sheria ambazo anga na dunia zinapaswa kufuata. Bado zinasimama.

decisions.choice: if I have not made my covenant: another impossible condition
decisions.reason: As in verse 20. God has set day and night and the laws of heaven and earth in place; as surely as he has, he will keep his promise to his people (verse 26). The verb "set" stands at the end and serves both halves of the verse.

decisions.choice: the fixed laws of heaven and earth: the order God gave creation
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for statutes. In 31:35-36 God speaks of "the fixed laws" of moon and stars: only if they failed would Israel cease to be a nation. Compare Job 38:33.

decisions.choice: statements in place of the condition
decisions.reason: Readable states what God has done and adds "They still stand", so that verse 26 can draw the comparison plainly. The meaning of the oath-like condition is kept.

source.text: גַּם־זֶ֣רַע יַעֲקוֹב֩ וְדָוִ֨ד עַבְדִּ֜י אֶמְאַ֗ס מִקַּ֤חַת מִזַּרְעוֹ֙ מֹֽשְׁלִ֔ים אֶל־זֶ֥רַע אַבְרָהָ֖ם יִשְׂחָ֣ק וְיַעֲקֹ֑ב כִּֽי־אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־שְׁבוּתָ֖ם וְרִחַמְתִּֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: also [the] offspring of Jacob and David my servant I will reject, from taking from his offspring rulers over [the] offspring of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; for I will turn back their fortunes and I will have compassion on them.

en.L: then also I would reject the offspring of Jacob and of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, so as not to take from his offspring rulers over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes, and I will have compassion on them."
en.B: then I would also reject Jacob's descendants and those of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, and not take rulers from David's line to govern the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Indeed, I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them."
en.R: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Jacob and of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David. I will always choose rulers from David's descendants to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I will make things good again for them, and I will have mercy on them."

es.L: también desecharía la descendencia de Jacob y de David {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo, para no tomar de su descendencia gobernantes sobre la descendencia de Abraham, de Isaac y de Jacob. Porque yo restauraré su suerte, y tendré compasión de ellos».
es.B: entonces también desecharía a los descendientes de Jacob y a los de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David, y no tomaría gobernantes del linaje de David para que gobernaran a los descendientes de Abraham, Isaac y Jacob. Pero de cierto restauraré su suerte y tendré compasión de ellos».
es.R: De la misma manera, nunca desecharé a los descendientes de Jacob y de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo David. Siempre escogeré gobernantes de entre los descendientes de David para que gobiernen a los descendientes de Abraham, Isaac y Jacob. decisions.choice: then I would reject: the result of the impossible condition
decisions.reason: As in verse 21: since the laws of creation stand, God will not reject Jacob's descendants or David's, and he will go on taking rulers from David's line.

decisions.choice: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: the promise to the fathers
decisions.reason: The rulers from David's line will rule over the people descended from the three fathers to whom God first made his covenant (Genesis 17:7; Exodus 2:24). The name Isaac is spelled here with a different letter, as in Amos 7:9, 16 and Psalm 105:9.

decisions.choice: restore their fortunes and have compassion: the promise of verse 7
decisions.reason: As in verse 7 and Deuteronomy 30:3, where the same two promises stand together. Compassion is the tender love of a parent for a child (31:20).

decisions.choice: I will restore: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a slightly different form of the verb "restore" from the one the scribes noted in the margin to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: Indeed (B)
decisions.reason: The small word that begins the last clause can mean "for" or "surely". Balanced says "Indeed", since the clause says what God will do in place of rejecting his people. Readable leaves the word out and says "make things good again" as in verse 7.
